Should I start saving for a house down payment?

Yes, if owning a home is a real goal, start saving for the down payment now. A down payment target is typically 20% of the price; saving early buys time and optionality (waiting for a better market, moving cities, or avoiding PMI).

I am saving $1000 a month, what should I do with it

Split it with one clear priority: pay high-interest debt first; that’s the best guaranteed return. Next, build or top up an emergency fund until you have 3–6 months of essentials. After that, prioritize any employer 401(k) match, then retirement accounts (IRA or 401k) up to useful limits, and finally taxable investing.

Should I pay off my credit card or invest?

Pay off the credit card first if it’s high-interest, that guaranteed savings beats typical market returns. If the card rate is low or you’re getting an employer match on retirement contributions, prioritize contributing just enough to capture the full match, then attack the card. After the card is cleared, shift extra money to investing or retirement.

what is a Roth IRA?

A Roth IRA is a retirement account you fund with after-tax dollars; your contributions grow tax-free and qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free. Contributions can be withdrawn any time without tax or penalty, earnings are tax-free if you’re 59½ and the account is at least five years old, and 2026 contribution limit is $7,500 (plus $1,100 catch-up if 50+).
